topic.title: How a Fed rate move travels from Washington to your credit card balance

title: When the Fed moves rates, how fast does your credit card follow?
description: The Fed raised the top of its target range to 4% in September and meets again this month. Here is how a quarter-point move reaches a $6,000 card balance at 22% a year. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Know your card's APR before the Fed meets

lines.text: When the Fed moves interest rates, how fast does your credit card follow?
In September, the Fed raised its target range by a quarter point, to 4% at the top.
Banks move their prime rate with it. And most card rates are prime plus a margin.
So within a billing cycle or two, your rate moves too.
Say you carry $6,000 at 22%. A quarter point more makes it 22.25%.
Paying only the minimum, the total interest goes from $7,948 to $8,172.
Small on its own. But every move stacks on the last one.
So, do you know your card's rate?
